data.hook: Ricursive's Ripple-65B Preview leads, with a $32M training-cost claim and a company-reported benchmark lead.
data.outro: Find full sources and links for every story on our website.

stories.headline: Ricursive releases Ripple-65B Preview, an open-weight model it says cost $32M to develop
stories.summary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview on November 12, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model behind its AI chip design platform. Ricursive says the dense Transformer was pretrained on 12 trillion tokens, supports up to 1M context, and is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, OpenRouter and Fireworks. The company says the model scored 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, ahead of several open-weight rivals, and that its full R&D cost was $32M.
stories.why_it_matters: Developers choosing open-weight models for coding agents may weigh Ricursive's claimed low training cost and its claim that the model runs on local hardware such as NVIDIA DGX Spark.
stories.limitations: Benchmark results are company-reported and not independently verified, and the cost and efficiency figures are also Ricursive's own.
stories.card_text: Ricursive's Ripple-65B Preview: open weights, $32M claimed R&D cost
stories.narration: Ricursive says its new open-weight model, Ripple-65B Preview, scored eighty point five two on TerminalBench two point one. The company says it spent thirty-two million dollars on full research and development. Those results have not been independently verified.

stories.headline: ReTrace turns agent runs into workflows where code, not an LLM, picks each step
stories.summary: Researchers present ReTrace, a method that turns a standard operating procedure and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow. The authors say LLM agents call a model to choose every step, which adds latency and cost at scale, and ReTrace lets code select the next step instead. In their reported tests on 79 procedures, ReTrace workflows reached 93.8% completion versus 96.8% for the agent, at 24% lower cost per task.
stories.why_it_matters: Teams running many automated business procedures could cut cost per task and latency if coded workflows keep most of an agent's accuracy.
stories.limitations: Results are reported by the authors and not independently verified, and ReTrace trailed the agent on completion and task success in the reported tests.
stories.card_text: ReTrace: coded workflows replace LLM step-picking, at 24% lower cost per task
stories.narration: Researchers present ReTrace, which turns agent runs into workflows where code, not a language model, chooses each step. The authors say it cuts cost per task by twenty-four percent, though it trails the agent slightly on accuracy.

stories.headline: LeRobot v0.7.0 adds streamed-data training and interactive robot control
stories.summary: Hugging Face says LeRobot v0.7.0 lets users train on datasets streamed from the Hub, a Storage Bucket or LanceDB without downloading them first. The release also adds interactive rollouts for switching subtasks and steering a running robot from the terminal, plus four world action models and four new VLA models. The Hub now hosts almost 300 TB of open physical AI data in LeRobot format.
stories.why_it_matters: Robotics developers can train on large open datasets without local copies, and run policies on a remote GPU while the robot's own computer handles cameras and motors.
stories.limitations: Speed gains are company-reported and not independently verified, and G0.5 is released under a non-commercial license rather than Apache-2.0.
stories.card_text: LeRobot v0.7.0: train on streamed data, steer robots from the terminal
stories.narration: Hugging Face says LeRobot version zero point seven lets robotics developers train on streamed datasets without downloading them first. It also adds interactive control, so users can steer a running robot from the terminal.

stories.headline: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom partner on Korean sovereign AI infrastructure
stories.summary: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a collaboration to advance Korea's sovereign AI infrastructure using NVIDIA NVLink Fusion. NVIDIA says the technology lets chipmakers combine specialized silicon with its scale-up networking, and Rebellions will connect its Rebel R200 NPUs to the NVIDIA platform using the MGX rack architecture. SK Telecom plans to deploy the systems in its AI data center, and the companies plan disaggregated inference with NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode.
stories.why_it_matters: Korean operators such as SK Telecom would deploy these systems, expanding domestic options for AI infrastructure built with local NPU chips alongside NVIDIA hardware.
stories.limitations: The R200 systems are not expected to be ready for deployment until 2028, so the plans are not yet in production.
stories.card_text: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom: NPUs and GPUs for Korean sovereign AI
stories.narration: NVIDIA says its NVLink Fusion technology will connect Korean chipmaker Rebellions' R200 processors to its platform. SK Telecom plans to deploy the systems in its AI data center. The R200 systems are expected to be ready in twenty twenty-eight.

stories.headline: UK sovereign AI fund and British Business Bank back chip startup Fractile
stories.summary: The UK Government's Sovereign AI Venture Fund and the British Business Bank have backed Fractile, a London and Bristol-based AI chip startup, in a Series C round worth over £500 million. The government says the round values Fractile at over £5 billion and that the company is rebuilding AI hardware to be faster, more energy efficient and less costly. Investors include CapitalG, Lightspeed and Redpoint, and the government's individual investment amounts are not disclosed.
stories.why_it_matters: The government says the investment could reduce reliance on overseas technology for UK companies that depend on AI hardware.
stories.limitations: The government's individual investment amounts are not disclosed, so the size of its stake is unknown.
stories.card_text: UK backs Fractile, valued at over £5 billion in a £500 million-plus round
stories.narration: The UK government and the British Business Bank have backed Fractile, a London and Bristol AI chip startup. The government says the round values the company at over five billion pounds.
